To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The quality of education is the single most important factor in improving student achievement; (2) Quality and equity in education are inextricably linked; and (3) Equity is a prerequisite to quality education.
the quality of the education system is determined more by the school culture and the quality of the teachers than by spending per student or the amount of money spent on the school.
equity and quality are important for all students, and equity and quality are the responsibility of the entire school community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the key issues of equity and quality in education?
the importance of equity as it relates to the quality of education for children.
how to improve the quality of education and reduce educational inequity in schools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quality education and equity in education are not mutually exclusive, but rather are mutually inclusive, as the two are interwoven.
equity and quality in education is the best investment a society can make in children.
the research findings of this study support the need for educational equity and quality in all K 12 schools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the research supports the need for a holistic approach to educational equity and quality that includes the school, the home, and the community working together to provide a quality education for all students.
the OECD report is an excellent reference to support the need for equity and quality in education.
the quality of education in schools can be enhanced by providing equity to all students and that equity can be provided through the use of instructional practices and a positive school culture.

we must continue to invest in children's early years and that we must invest in the quality of education in schools.
equity and quality education are important in K 12 school settings.
